messages:
maria: Hi team, escalating customer: their private service endpoint in consumer VPC intermittently resolves to the wrong IP or NXDOMAIN after we changed an internal hosted zone yesterday. App failing with 502s. Help?
ryan: Can you share the dig output + which VPCs are associated with the hosted zones?
maria: Repro steps below and outputs. Customer says it started ~5m after our Route53 change.

maria: REPRO STEPS:
1) From customer EC2 in consumer-vpc: `dig srv.api.svc.internal +short`
2) Sometimes returns nothing, other times returns private IP of legacy-hostedzone.svc.private (wrong zone)
3) Tried again after TTL and saw same

maria: dig output (snippet):
```
; dig srv.api.svc.internal A +short
# attempt 1 -> NXDOMAIN
; EOF
; dig srv.api.svc.internal A +short
# attempt 2 -> 10.10.22.8
; dig srv.api.svc.internal SOA +short
# response: ns-aws-route53
```

maria: aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name shows two private hosted zones with similar names and overlapping record sets: `svc.internal` (hosted-zone-aaaa) and `svc.internal` (hosted-zone-bbbb). We deployed a record change to hosted-zone-aaaa at 2026-03-10T12:04:22Z (change-id: C1234) and later associated it with provider-vpc. Customer is in consumer-vpc.

devin: Do we have a VPC association to consumer-vpc for the updated zone? If not, resolver will still match the older zone that's associated.
maria: Only hosted-zone-bbbb is associated with consumer-vpc currently (legacy). We intended to switch to hosted-zone-aaaa and then remove bbbb association, but it looks like the association step failed for consumer-vpc in the change runbook.

ryan: That explains split-horizon. If two private hosted zones share the same name, which one a resolver returns depends on VPC associations and cache. The intermittent NXDOMAIN/wrong-IP pattern is consistent with a mix of stale resolver cache entries and different upstream answers.

maria: Customer's kube-proxy and node-local dns are returning cached answers per pod logs. Sample from node-local: `2026-03-10T12:10:18Z cache hit srv.api.svc.internal -> 10.10.22.8 ttl=22s` but other times there is cache miss and NXDOMAIN.

alex: Any quick mitigation for the customer while we fix associations?
devin: Options:
- Associate hosted-zone-aaaa with consumer-vpc (if permitted) so the new zone is authoritative immediately.
- Or remove association of hosted-zone-bbbb from consumer-vpc (but that requires change windows).
- Flush node-local caches on their nodes: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l k8s-app=node-local-dns` or `systemctl restart nodelocaldns` on instances.

maria: Tried flushing node-local, but services still see NXDOMAIN intermittently. I suspect resolver caches at the VPC resolver or shared forwarder level.

ryan: Check VPC resolver rules and any shared forwarder (transit VPC / firewall appliance) TTL caching. Use: `aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id hosted-zone-aaaa` and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id hosted-zone-aaaa` to confirm VPCs.

maria: Ran `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id hosted-zone-aaaa` output includes: `VPCs: [{VPCId: vpc-aaa, Region: us-west-2}]` only. hosted-zone-bbbb lists consumer-vpc (vpc-ccc).

maria: So the new zone is not associated to consumer-vpc yet (bug in automation). Ops will run association now. Change command: 
```
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id hosted-zone-aaaa --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-ccc
```

ryan: After assoc, there can still be cached responses for up to the previous TTL on intermediate caches. For immediate relief, either: flush caches (node-local, forwarders) OR create temporary CNAME in hosted-zone-bbbb that points to the correct record (not ideal).

devin: Also check if the resolver endpoint in consumer account has an outbound forwarder that adds its own caching layer (e.g., squid/HAProxy). Those often have long TTLs.
maria: Customer confirmed they have a FortiGate forwarder that caches DNS for 60s by default. They're flushing it now.

route53-bot: Change C1234 (hosted-zone-aaaa) status: INSYNC at 2026-03-10T12:14:02Z

maria: I ran the associate command; AWS returned asociate request accepted. We'll monitor.

ryan: Please collect `dig +trace srv.api.svc.internal` from the customer before and after assoc so we can see which resolver returns which zone. Also capture any firewall forwarder logs.

maria: Will do. Customer ran `dig +short` again and got 10.10.22.8 after assoc. Later they still saw one pod report NXDOMAIN but most pods resolved correctly.

devin: Follow-up actions:
- Confirm hosted-zone-bbbb disassociated from consumer-vpc once traffic stable (avoid duplicate zones).
- Add a preflight check to the automation to verify VPC association success and retry on failure.
- Add runbook note to flush known forwarders (FortiGate, node-local) after private zone swap to reduce split-horizon window.

maria: Filing platform ticket to update automation and runbook, linking customer case 2026-1428. I'll keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks, team. Customer is ok for now but wants a postmortem on steps to avoid recurrence.

ryan: I'll own the postmortem with ops and dev. Assigning to eng-infra for the automation fix.

maria: Closing interim support loop — will reopen if we see full regression.
